aldemar.headline: Gold screams what the tape whispers — and Intel closes below its own offering
aldemar.standfirst: Wednesday looked calm on the surface — S&P +0.21% to 7,708, VIX back to 15.05 — while gold rose 4.6% to a record near 4,569, its biggest day of the year, on the day the Fed's minutes landed. A haven moving like that on a green equity day is the war being priced somewhere other than stocks: Trump flatly denied Kushner's "very positive and active conversations", announced a "crushing economic operation" against Iran instead, two Iranian ballistic missiles landed in the water off the UAE, and Hormuz transits fell 19.5% in a week. In the book, Aldemar's INTC closed at 92.80 — below the $95 the new shares cleared on Tuesday — and BAC took a policy counterpunch to the steepener.

positions.title: 2 signals on BAC, INTC — read before the open

items.html: BAC — Treasury doubles its long-bond buyback limit — the 10-year drops to 4.65% and banks sell off, BAC −1.65% to 63.17. This is a policy action aimed straight at the mechanism your thesis rides: official buying at the long end pulls exactly the yields whose rise was widening bank margins, and financials were sold as a group the moment it landed. One intervention does not end a steepener driven by deficits and $90 oil, but it is the first genuine counterpunch. Gabriel is −1.88% on entry at −0.30R, stop at 60.39 (4.6% below current); Aldemar −1.54% at −0.22R, stop 59.65. The 62 support zone from the original thesis is now 1.9% below — that level, not 65, is this week's line.

INTC — INTC −4.0% to 92.80 — a close below the $95 offering price, on tepid OpenAI results hitting the whole complex. Two sessions after $20B of new stock cleared at $95, the market marked it under the buyers' cost basis — that is weak sponsorship, and it converts $95 from support into the level longs are trapped at. The day's driver was sector-wide (AMD fell the same ~4% on soft OpenAI numbers), so the CPU-inference thesis was not specifically refuted. Aldemar is −12.3% on entry at −0.53R — just over half the risk unit spent — with the 81.10 stop 12.6% below and the 142.75 target built for exactly this kind of drawdown. The wide-stop design is being used as designed; the only question that matters is the one already answered at entry: the stop is the exit, nothing before it.

positions.note: Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size — earnings, a regulator with teeth, M&A, a ruling with a revenue line attached. Everything else is filed as noise on purpose; a real signal survives skepticism.

themes.right: no talks · missiles off the UAE · Hormuz transits −19.5%
themes.title: Kushner says talks are active, Trump says there are none — the missiles say Tehran isn't waiting

items.html: Trump: "no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled" — contradicting his own envoy within the day, and announcing a "crushing economic operation" on Iran. Kushner had described "very positive and active conversations" this week; the public correction chooses escalation on the financial track over the diplomatic one. For markets the operative word is operation — sanctions machinery of unseen scale is now the stated plan, which is supply-negative for oil at the margin.

UAE detects two Iranian ballistic missiles landing in its waters; a ship in the strait struck by an unknown projectile, one casualty. Missiles into Gulf-state waters — even ones that hit nothing — widen the theatre beyond the blockade line, and the projectile strike adds a casualty to commercial shipping's ledger. War-risk premiums for the whole Gulf reprice off this, not off communiqués.

Strait traffic down 19.5% in a week to 95 transits. The quantity signal keeps deteriorating faster than the rhetoric changes. Roughly one in five transits has vanished in seven days — that is supply physically not moving, the input the inflation math cannot ignore.

Araghchi: Iran "will not accept a ceasefire; the war must come to an end" — Hormuz reopens only when the blockade and sanctions lift. Tehran has moved past truce-seeking to total-settlement terms while Washington demands surrender. Both endgames require the other side to fold first; nothing in between is on offer.

themes.note: The transmission is oil → inflation → the regime call, but Wednesday added a second channel: gold. A 4.6% single-day rise to a record, on a day equities were green and the VIX fell, is the market buying insurance against a prolonged-inflation-shock outcome without selling stocks to do it. Crude itself eased 0.9% to 84.21 — positioning noise after four straight gains, not a change of view, with Brent holding the $90 handle. CPI y/y stands at 3.3 against the 2.5 floor and the war is now structurally holding that gate open. Watch gold, not the wire: if it keeps this bid through OPEX on Friday, the hedgers know something the tape is not saying yet.

world.title: A record-adjacent tape, a record gold price, and minutes that mention hikes

items.html: FOMC minutes show some policymakers still see rate hikes as possibly appropriate this year; Treasury doubles long-bond buyback limits. A hawkish minority on paper, a dovish action in practice — the buyback expansion pulled the 10-year to 4.65% and the 30-year off its 2007 highs. The bond market took the intervention over the rhetoric, and so did gold.

Gold +4.6% to a record ~4,569 — the year's biggest single-day move. Rate-hike odds cooling, a war with no exit, and official intervention in the bond market is the full debasement-trade recipe. Gold rising with stocks green and the VIX falling is the same unusual pairing the edition flagged on 7 August — at triple the size.

Chips fall on tepid OpenAI results — Intel and AMD both ~−4%. The AI-financing audit gained a demand-side exhibit: it is no longer only how the build-out is funded, but what the flagship customer's numbers say about what the build-out earns. The read-across pressure now runs both directions.

S&P +0.21% to 7,708, Nasdaq marginally mixed, VIX −5% to 15.05; Moderna +177% on a vaccine-trial success; retail gains on earnings. Beneath a flat surface: banks and AI infrastructure sold, pharma and retail bought. Rotation is doing all the work while the index stands still — and Friday's OPEX removes the pin that has kept it standing still.

weekly.headline: The week the market started auditing the AI bill — and the war stopped pretending
weekly.standfirst: Five sessions, a third straight weekly gain, and a record close on Thursday: the S&P added 0.36% to 7,785.76 while the VIX fell to 14.25. Underneath that calm, two things changed. Investors began pricing how AI infrastructure is financed rather than what it might earn — Alphabet on Tuesday, Broadcom and Applied Materials on Friday — while the CPU side of the same trade got re-rated upward. And the war moved from rhetoric to enforcement: a US helicopter disabled a tanker running the blockade, Hormuz traffic sank to three-month lows, and the interim deal now expires on Tuesday.

Two inflation prints cooled, one consumer cracked, and the AI trade split in half

TECHThe AI capex audit begins: GOOG −3.6% Tuesday on a $25bn bond deal, AVGO −6% Friday on a $370bn financing question. Alphabet's quarterly capex hit $44.9bn with free cash flow negative for the first time; Broadcom was marked down on how a lease-and-debt structure gets funded. The market spent this week deciding that the cost of the build belongs in the valuation.TradingKey · Yahoo Finance · 11–14 Aug
SEMISBofA lifts the 2030 CPU market from $170bn to $210bn — INTC ran 6.3% Thursday before fading 2.0% Friday. Vivek Arya's argument is that AI moving from training to inference resets the GPU-to-CPU ratio toward 1:1. It is the bull case for both INTC positions, and Friday showed it will not travel in a straight line.Motley Fool · BofA · 13 Aug
DATACPI cooled Wednesday, PPI cooled Thursday to 4.7% from 5.5%, then retail sales fell 0.6% Friday. Three prints that moved September from a coin flip to a hold. The tone changed midweek: the first two were disinflation, the third was demand weakening — the same direction with a very different meaning for earnings.BLS · AP · 12–14 Aug
RATESThe 30-year auction clears at 5.216% — the highest in a quarter century. The long end refused to follow the cooler prints down, which is a fiscal and energy verdict rather than a policy one. It is the single cleanest reason to be long a bank here.Yahoo Finance · 14 Aug
NOISEFiled and ignored: Pixel 11 previews, an Alphabet 11-year retrospective, a $107.66 Intel target already overtaken. A week's worth of commentary that arrived after the moves it described. None of it touched a thesis, a level or a size.various · 10–14 Aug

The through-line is that this market has stopped paying for AI ambition and started pricing AI arithmetic — who is writing the cheques versus who is cashing them. You now hold one of each: Alphabet writing them, Intel cashing them.

From rhetoric to Hellfire missiles in five sessions

STRIKEA US Navy helicopter disables the M/V Vela Nova with two Hellfire missiles in the Gulf of Oman. The first commercial vessel fired on since the ceasefire, and the moment the blockade stopped being a declaration. Engine room and steering gear, deliberately disabling rather than sinking.12 Aug
SHIPPINGHormuz traffic falls to near three-month lows as both sides claim control. Trump says the strait is open under US control; Iran says nothing passes without its permission. The traffic data settles it — whoever is right, the tankers are not sailing.13 Aug
MILITARYHegseth: the blockade can hold "indefinitely"; a relief carrier group sails Friday. Words backed by a rotation schedule. The market's hope that enforcement fades on its own was removed this week.13–14 Aug
OILWTI rose 4.7% on the week to 81.84 while equities made a record. Energy finished as the week's best sector. Crude is carrying the war risk that the equity indices are not.10–14 Aug

The week's arc runs from talks-are-close on Monday to a missile strike on Tuesday to annexation talk on Friday. Nothing was signed, and the June interim deal now expires on Tuesday 18 August with the blockade live and both sides demanding compensation from the other.

INTC 105 is its put wall and Friday closed below it; reclaiming it matters more than the noise around it. GOOG sits on its gamma flip near 344, where hedging switches from dampening to amplifying.Mon 17 Aug

Two of the three positions are less than one session old, so the working assumption into Monday is patience: the entries were made against levels, and none of those levels has been tested yet.
